answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed riverside forge built on one named ledge, where the holder smelts ferrous ore into tools for real buyers under a master smith who inspects one forge per day. Random checks summon the holder to strike that exact anvil live within minutes, and one smith cannot work two forges at once. The forge license fee, paid in outside money, doubles for each further identity on the same funding trail, so every extra fake costs another real forge, another season of smithing, another human, and twice the prior fee.
